name: Hall of Pillars
read: Eight thick stone pillars hold up the ceiling of this square hall, and the slate floor is wet and dotted with puddles. Glistening trails of slime wind between the pillars, and torn leathery sacs, each as large as a barrel, lie split open among scattered bones. Something pale and swollen moves in the shadows behind the pillars.
notes:
The entrance hall of the tomb. The entrance double door opens into it from the east. The torn sacs are the hatched egg sacs of the Corpse Worm's larvae, and the slime trails are theirs.

A secret door in the west wall opens onto a short passage that ends in an arch into the Hidden Vestry (room 2). A DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check finds it.

The arch in the south wall leads into a corridor that runs south to the Chamber of the Mouth (room 3). Off that corridor, a secret door in the west wall opens into the Hidden Vestry (room 2), and a side passage runs west and ends in a secret door onto the West Passage. A DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check finds each secret door.

Encounter (Power Level 8, Durability 15)

Five Venom Grub larvae, each the size of a horse, feed on the bones behind the pillars. They crawl out and attack as soon as a creature enters the hall.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing lies among the bones, in the pack of a dead tomb robber.

Exits: Hidden Vestry (2, secret door), Chamber of the Mouth (3, arch). The corridor south to room 3 also has a secret door into the Hidden Vestry (2) and a side passage that ends in a secret door onto the West Passage. The entrance double door in the east wall leads out into the marsh.

name: Hidden Vestry
read: Mouldering robes hang from pegs along the walls of this narrow room, and a stone shelf holds a small iron coffer. On a hook beside the shelf hangs a silver key with a bow shaped like a curled tongue.
notes:
The vestry where the Storm Witch's servants kept her robes and the key to the Mouth. The bandits, cultists and other owners who held the tomb after her never found this room.

The silver key is the Silver Tongue Key. It opens the Mouth in the Chamber of the Mouth (room 3) without triggering the Biting Mouth trap.

The iron coffer is locked. A DC 15 Dexterity check with thieves' tools opens it, or a DC 15 Strength check breaks it open.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Silver Tongue Key (story item; it opens the Mouth in room 3 safely) on the hook, and a Wand of Magic Missiles and 300 gp in the iron coffer.

Exits: Hall of Pillars (1, arch), Hall of Pillars (1, secret door), Stair Cell (4, door). The arch leads to the secret passage behind the west wall of room 1. The secret door opens onto the corridor between room 1 and the Chamber of the Mouth (room 3). The door in the west wall opens onto the West Passage, which leads to the Stair Cell (room 4) and on to the crossroads north of the Trunk Room (room 10).

name: Chamber of the Mouth
read: The western wall of this chamber is carved into a huge stone face, and its wide open mouth is a double door of stone set with rows of stone teeth. A faint violet light glows in the face's two stone eyes. Bones lie scattered on the floor in front of the mouth. A flight of stairs climbs into the east wall, and a plain door stands in the south wall.
notes:
Watabou note: A mouth-shaped double door on the western wall.

The Mouth is the Storm Witch's guarded gate. It is a locked double door. The Silver Tongue Key from the Hidden Vestry (room 2) opens it safely. The lock can be picked (DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools) or the door forced (DC 18 Strength check), but either one triggers the Biting Mouth. The bones belong to people who tried.

Beyond the Mouth, a straight passage runs south to the junction north of the Crypt of the Wormridden (room 5). There are two longer ways to the same junction that do not need the key. The stairs in the east wall climb into a winding passage that ends at the junction. The door in the south wall opens onto stairs that end at a secret door onto the junction; a DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check finds it from the stair side.

Trap: Biting Mouth

  • Trigger: a creature standing in front of the Mouth opens or forces the double door without the Silver Tongue Key.
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) notices that the stone teeth are hinged and that the jaw is set to close.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 piercing]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, held in the stone jaws until it or an ally uses an action and succeeds on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
  • Disarm or avoid: Use the Silver Tongue Key, or wedge the jaws open with an iron bar or crowbar before opening the door (DC 16 Strength (Athletics)), or open the door from out of reach with a rope or mage hand so that no creature stands in front of it.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Hall of Pillars (1, open passage), Crypt of the Wormridden (5, locked double door), Crypt of the Wormridden (5, stairs), Crypt of the Wormridden (5, door). The open way north is the corridor to room 1. The locked double door is the Mouth. The stairs lead through the winding passage, and the south door leads down the stairs to the secret door; all three reach the junction north of room 5.

name: Stair Cell
read: A stone bench lies toppled in this small, bare cell, beside a cracked copper bowl. Wet footprints cross the floor toward the stairs, and a rusted lantern sits in the corner.
notes:
A watch cell for the servants who guarded the West Passage. The wet footprints are the first sign of the Drowned Knights. They lead to the stairs and fade on the dry stone of the West Passage.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Hidden Vestry (2, stairs). The stairs lead up to the West Passage, which runs to the Hidden Vestry (room 2), to the side passage that ends in a secret door near the Hall of Pillars (room 1), and west to the crossroads north of the Trunk Room (room 10).

name: Crypt of the Wormridden
read: Burial niches line the walls of this long crypt, and every one of them has burst open from the inside. Round holes as wide as a man's shoulders are bored into the walls and floor, and slime and torn burial wrappings cover everything. Shapes in rotting wrappings stand among the broken niches, swaying.
notes:
The crypt of the Storm Witch's servants. The Corpse Worm's grubs bored through the walls and nested in the dead, and the dead rose.

Encounter (Power Level 9, Durability 16)

Four Wormridden Corpses stand among the niches. They lurch forward when the party enters, and grubs squirm under their skin.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in one of the burst niches.

Exits: Chamber of the Mouth (3, open passage), Hall of the Coven (6, door). The open way north leads to the junction where the Mouth passage, the winding passage and the secret door from room 3 meet.

name: Hall of the Coven
read: Statues of robed women lie toppled across the floor of this long hall, their stone faces turned up to the ceiling. Black scorch marks in the shape of branching lightning streak the walls and floor, and a cracked copper rod rises from a socket at the hall's centre. The air smells of a coming storm, and it is very cold.
notes:
The hall of the Storm Witch's coven. When she died, her coven sisters were bound here as her eternal guard. The copper rod is a lightning rod the coven used in their rites. It can be pulled from its socket (DC 13 Strength check) and used to ground the Storm Crevice in room 8.

Encounter (Power Level 10, Durability 16)

Four Tempest Wraiths rise from the toppled statues when the first creature reaches the middle of the hall. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Crypt of the Wormridden (5, door), Crevice of the Comb (8, open passage), Sunken Boathouse (7, open passage).

name: Sunken Boathouse
read: Shallow, murky water covers the floor of this chamber, and reeds grow up through it along the walls. The rotting hull of a small boat lies on its side in the water, with oars and coils of rope beside it. Stairs at the west end lead down into the dark.
notes:
The witch's boathouse, once open to the marsh by a water tunnel that has since collapsed. The water is 2 feet deep and is difficult terrain.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Climbing sits wedged under a seat in the boat hull.

Exits: Hall of the Coven (6, open passage), Knights' Rest (11, stairs).

name: Crevice of the Comb
read: A jagged crevice splits the floor of this chamber, and a cold blue light glows from deep inside it. Broken pottery is scattered across the floor, and a cracked stone table stands against one wall.
notes:
Watabou note: A magic comb hidden in a crevice of the floor.

The Storm Witch kept her stored storm magic in this crevice, and she hid her comb inside it. The comb lies on a ledge in the crevice, within arm's reach of the edge at the room's centre.

Trap: Storm Crevice

  • Trigger: a creature reaches into or steps over the glowing crevice at the room's centre.
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) recognizes the blue light as stored lightning.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 lightning]] on a failure, half on a success.
  • Disarm or avoid: Ground the charge by setting a length of metal into the crevice so that it touches the stone, such as the copper rod from the Hall of the Coven (room 6), or cast dispel magic (DC 15), or take the comb with mage hand.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Storm Witch's Comb (common: hair combed with it stays dry and neat in any weather; as a Bonus Action you can comb a creature's hair to end the Deafened condition on it) on the ledge in the crevice.

Exits: Hall of the Coven (6, open passage), Trunk Room (10, stairs).

name: Lair of the Corpse Worm
read: A huge stone sarcophagus lies smashed in the centre of this vast chamber, and great round burrows open in the floor and walls around it. A coiled, papery shed skin as long as a ship lies along one wall, and pools of green venom gleam among piles of bones and bodies. In the dark beyond the sarcophagus, a pale green-white light glows and slowly moves.
notes:
The burial chamber of the Storm Witch and the end of the adventure. The Corpse Worm burrowed up into it from below, smashed the sarcophagus and swallowed Soride, the Storm Lantern. The light is Soride, shining through the worm's rotting hide.

A secret door in the south-west corner leads to the Witch's Study (room 12). A DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check finds it from this side.

Encounter (Power Level 12, Durability 18)

The Corpse Worm and two Wormridden Corpses. The Corpse Worm is an Epic Boss with 550 Hit Points: it never rolls initiative, acts on initiative count 10, and takes one Response after each player character's turn. The Wormridden Corpses climb out of the piles of bodies when it attacks.

When the Corpse Worm dies, Soride can be cut from its body.

Treasure: Soride, the Storm Lantern (story item; inside the worm), the Wand of Lightning Bolts (the witch's own wand) in the smashed sarcophagus, and 500 gp among the bones.

Exits: Trunk Room (10, stairs), Witch's Study (12, secret door). The stairs wind down to the crossroads north of the Trunk Room (room 10).

name: Trunk Room
read: A broken wooden trunk stands in the middle of this small room, spilling old clothes across the floor. A long grey scarf hangs over its edge. Cobwebs fill the corners, and an oil lamp lies tipped over beside the trunk.
notes:
Watabou note: A broken trunk holds a scarf.

A trunk of clothes left by one of the tomb's later owners. One of the cultists hexed it to protect his belongings.

The open way north leads to a stair passage and a crossroads. West, stairs lead to the Witch's Study (room 12) and the Painted Gallery (room 13). North, winding stairs lead up to the Lair of the Corpse Worm (room 9). East, the long West Passage runs back to the Stair Cell (room 4), the Hidden Vestry (room 2) and the side passage that ends in a secret door near the Hall of Pillars (room 1).

Trap: Hexed Trunk

  • Trigger: a creature steps up to the broken trunk in the middle of the room.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices faint green hex marks scratched into the trunk's lid.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition until it finishes a Short Rest.
  • Disarm or avoid: Cast dispel magic (DC 16), or hook the scarf or drag the trunk away with a pole or rope from at least 10 feet away.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Scarf of Clear Breath (common: while worn over the mouth you have Advantage on saving throws against inhaled gases and spores), the long grey scarf on the trunk.

Exits: Crevice of the Comb (8, stairs), Lair of the Corpse Worm (9, stairs), Witch's Study (12, stairs), Painted Gallery (13, stairs), Stair Cell (4, open passage). All but the first are reached through the open way north and the crossroads.

name: Knights' Rest
read: Six stone biers stand in two rows down this long, damp hall. On each lies an armored knight under a blanket of green pondweed, a rusted sword and shield at its side. A small iron chest sits at the foot of the far bier. Water drips steadily from the ceiling.
notes:
The resting place of the knights who defeated the Storm Witch. With her dying curse she flooded the tomb and drowned them, and they rose as Drowned Knights, bound to guard her tomb against everyone. Two of the six biers are empty; those knights stand in the Witch's Study (room 12).

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 17)

Four Drowned Knights rise from the biers when a creature reaches the middle of the hall, water pouring from their armor. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: a Javelin of Lightning and 600 gp in the small iron chest, the knights' war chest.

Exits: Sunken Boathouse (7, stairs).

name: Witch's Study
read: A heavy stone desk stands in this chamber, buried under rotting books and scrolls. A crystal orb lies smashed on the floor among shelves of glass jars, and a star chart of storms is inlaid in the floor in silver. Armored figures and pale, drifting shapes stand among the shelves.
notes:
The Storm Witch's study. The star chart in the floor shows the seasons of the great marsh storms. Two Drowned Knights and two of her coven sisters still guard it, side by side.

A secret door in the north-east corner leads to the Lair of the Corpse Worm (room 9). A DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check finds it.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 16.5)

Two Drowned Knights and two Tempest Wraiths attack anyone who enters and fight until destroyed.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Trunk Room (10, stairs), Lair of the Corpse Worm (9, secret door), Drowned Chapel (14, door). The stairs lead east to the crossroads north of room 10.

name: Painted Gallery
read: Painted wooden boards lean against every wall of this chamber, showing the swamps around the tomb in murky greens and browns. The north wall itself is painted with a great swamp landscape. Spilled paint has dried on the floor around a broken easel.
notes:
Watabou note: A graffiti on the wall depicting the swamps around the tomb.

A mad painter lived here for a time, painting the marsh over and over. He left his boards, his paint and his easel behind. What happened to him is unknown.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Trunk Room (10, stairs), Hall of Storm Glyphs (15, door). The stairs lead east to the crossroads north of room 10.

name: Drowned Chapel
read: Broken stone pews lie in rows before a cracked altar carved with a copper lightning sigil. Water seeps down the walls and pools between the pews. Swaying corpses stand among the pews, and large pale grubs crawl over the altar.
notes:
The Storm Witch's chapel. The cultists who held the tomb after her worshipped here, and the grubs found them.

Encounter (Power Level 9, Durability 17)

Two Wormridden Corpses and three Venom Grub larvae attack together when the party enters.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing and a Cloak of Protection on the body of a dead cultist behind the altar.

Exits: Witch's Study (12, door), Hall of Storm Glyphs (15, open passage).

name: Hall of Storm Glyphs
read: A ring of copper runes is inlaid in the floor at the centre of this hall, and a faint blue glow plays over them. Scorch marks spread out from the ring across the floor and up the walls.
notes:
The hall where the Storm Witch called her storms. The ring still holds her power.

Trap: Storm Glyph Ring

  • Trigger: a creature steps into the ring of copper runes at the room's centre.
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) recognizes the ring as an active storm ward.
  • Effect: DC 16 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 thunder]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Walk around the ring, or cast dispel magic (DC 16).
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Painted Gallery (13, door), Drowned Chapel (14, open passage).
